newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: National Mutual makes A$3bln splash on share market.
newsitem.headline: National Mutual makes A$3bln splash on share market.

text.p: Australian life insurer National Mutual Holdings Ltd delighted its big army of shareholders with a strong debut on Australian and New Zealand bourses on Tuesday.
National Mutual shares closed A$1.80 or 20 percent above the level paid by retail investors and at a 13-percent premium to the price paid by institutional investors.

But the biggest winner of the day was French financial services giant Axa SA, which paid A$1.1 billion (US$870 million) for a 51-percent National Mutual stake last year. The stake was worth about A$1.60 billion on Tuesday.

"You would have to say if you were looking for a positive start, then this is about as positive as you could get, I would have thought," managing director Geoff Tomlinson told reporters after his company's shares listed.
National Mutual now has about 500,000 shareholders, giving it one of the biggest shareholder bases in Australia.
The sharemarket listing catapults National Mutual into the top 25 of Australia's listed companies with a market capitalisation of around A$3 billion at Tuesday's closing price.

National Mutual is expected to be joined on the stock exchange boards next year by fellow Melbourne-based insurer, the Colonial Mutual group. Last month Colonial unveiled plans to give A$1.3 billion worth of shares to its policy-holders.

Australian insurance analysts said National Mutual and Colonial would then be followed to the market by Australia's largest insurer and institutional investor, the Australian Mutual Provident Society (AMP), in a few years time.
"AMP will list, I would be very suprised if they don't," said one Sydney-based analyst.
AMP said in January it would look at a new corporate structure, with a sharemarket listing as one of its options.
A possible listing of AMP would be about double the size of National Mutual. AMP has total asset under management of about A$86 billion, compared with National Mutual's A$48 billion.
However, AMP is not expected to make any statement regarding its corporate structure until late this year or early 1997.

"We knew it was going to be a very complex and a very ongoing and long term project so we gave ourselves a decent time. We did say at least the fourth quarter so it could go into next year," said AMP spokesman James Willoughby.
Analysts said National Mutual shares were likely to remain around the A$1.80 levels since the offer had been six times oversubscribed and demand was high.
"I would think it is quite a good story," said Tony Jackson, an insurance analyst at Macquarie Equities.

Jackson said he expected National Mutual shares to be quite sought after as they had good exposure to Asia through the company's 69-percent stake in Hong Kong-based National Mutual Asia Ltd, the colony's second-largest insurer.
Insurance analysts said National Mutual's strong presence in Hong Kong could put it in a good position to get a licence to start activities in China.
The Chinese government is expected to issue a number of insurance licences next year to foreign companies.

National Mutual's listing completes its 21-month transition from a mutual company owned by its policyholders to a listed group free to pursue its strategic focus on Asia, unshackled by a mutual requirement to act solely in policyholders' interests.
